text: How many sides do four hexagons have altogether?
why: A hexagon has 6 sides: 4 × 6 = 24.

text: A team scores 2 goals before half-time and 3 after it, and lets in 4. By how many goals do they win?
why: They score 5 and let in 4.

text: A florist sells a dozen roses for £24. How much is that for each rose?
How many minutes are there in two and a half hours?
Share 99 sweets equally between three children. How many does each child get?
Unscramble RAMCH to find a month of the year.
why: R-A-M-C-H makes MARCH.

text: How many corners does a cube have?
why: Four on the top face and four on the bottom.

text: What gets wetter the more it dries?
why: A towel soaks up the water as it dries you.

text: What has a head and a tail but no body?
why: Heads or tails!

text: Add up the four angles inside a square. What do you get, in degrees?
why: Four right angles: 4 × 90 = 360.

text: How long is a quarter of an hour, counted in seconds?
why: 15 minutes × 60 seconds = 900.

text: Which month has the longest name, and how many letters is that?
why: SEPTEMBER has nine letters; no month has more.

text: A shop doubles all its prices, then holds a half-price sale. What does a £30 jumper cost in the sale?
why: Doubled to £60, then halved back to £30.

text: What is 25% of 25% of 160?
A triangle is cut by one straight line from a corner to the opposite side. How many triangles can you count now?
why: The two small ones, plus the big one they make together.

text: Cut a cake in half, halve one piece, then halve that piece again. What fraction of the whole cake is your piece?
why: ½ × ½ × ½ = ⅛.

text: Say 'silk' out loud three times. Now: what do cows drink?
why: Cows drink water; the silk makes you want to say milk.

text: How many birthdays does the average person have?
why: You're only born once: the rest are anniversaries of it.

text: Before Mount Everest was discovered, what was the highest mountain in the world?
why: It was still Everest, even before anyone measured it.

text: Half of a number is 4 more than a third of it. What is the number?
why: 12 is 4 more than 8: half of 24 and a third of 24.

text: Write out every number from 1 to 30. How many times do you write the digit 2?
why: 2, 12, 22 for the units, plus 20 to 29 for the tens: 3 + 10 = 13.

text: Apart from 1, what is the smallest whole number that is both a square number and a cube number?
Over twelve hours, how often do a clock's two hands form a perfect right angle?
why: Twice every hour, except around 3 and 9 where two of those moments fall together: 24 − 2 = 22.
